local.h: Exhibit traces Cassatt's lost World's Fair mural
local.b: A new exhibit tells the story of Mary Cassatt's three-panel 1893 World's Fair mural, last known to be in Chicago in 1912.
local.title: Painter Mary Cassatt created a masterpiece for the 1893 World’s Fair in Chicago. Then, it disappeared.

local.h: Southport Grocery to close Dec. 31
local.b: The Lake View breakfast spot, open since 2003, will make way for Dollop Finer Diner, an outpost of Dollop Coffee Co.

local.h: UChicago students rally after assault reports
local.b: More than 100 students called on the university to improve sexual assault prevention and survivor support after two cases tied to the campus in recent weeks.

local.b: Skidmore, Owings and Merrill released renderings of a domed Bears stadium and mixed-use district at Bridgeport's Rate Field, presented by Sterling Bay.

local.h: High tides speed up Palos Verdes landslide
local.b: Land in the Portuguese Bend area is moving more than an inch a week, up from August, after storm-fueled waves eroded the coast, city officials said.
local.title: Recent high tides worsen landslide activity in Rancho Palos Verdes

local.h: California high-speed rail CEO resigns
local.b: Ian Choudri cited personal and family priorities after a tenure troubled by budget woes, delays and the misuse of nearly $600,000 for questionable trips.
local.title: Head of California high-speed rail agency resigns amid travel expenses scandal

local.h: Bass and feds disagree on MacArthur Park arrests
local.b: Mayor Karen Bass said she had not approved arresting people for using drugs in the park; a federal prosecutor who oversaw the operation said she did.
local.title: Who approved arresting people for using drugs at MacArthur Park? Bass and feds disagree

local.h: Judge keeps LAHSA suspension on hold
local.b: U.S. District Judge David O. Carter's order lets federal homelessness money keep flowing through LAHSA while it hands its federal roles to L.A. County.
local.title: Judge keeps Trump suspension of LAHSA on hold as key homelessness roles shift to LA County

local.h: LA leaders mourn Dolores Huerta
local.b: Local leaders honored the United Farm Workers co-founder's legacy as a dedicated advocate for workers' and women's rights after her death Wednesday.

goodnews.h: Cole's French Dip set to return
goodnews.b: New owners Sean Maloney and Jeremy Fall plan to reopen the iconic downtown LA restaurant, which closed in March, by Thanksgiving.
goodnews.title: The return of Cole’s French Dip

local.h: Nobody is enforcing NYC's $3 bus fare for now
local.b: Enforcement is on pause after a series of confrontations involving MTA agents, and the NYPD will not step in while the security force is suspended.
local.title: NYPD won't enforce NYC's bus fare while MTA security force is suspended

local.h: Garbage truck kills woman in Brooklyn
local.b: Siobhan Lynch, 30, was struck by a Department of Sanitation truck while crossing Bay Parkway at Cropsey Avenue Wednesday evening, the NYPD said.
local.title: Brooklyn woman hit and killed by garbage truck at Bay Parkway, NYPD says

local.h: Woman charged with hate crimes in stabbings of Jewish men
local.b: Federal prosecutors accuse Anna Mochalova, 32, of stabbing two Jewish men near the Diamond District with a sharp object consistent with a needle.
local.title: Woman charged with federal hate crimes after allegedly stabbing 2 Jewish men in NYC

local.h: E-bike battery caused fatal Bronx fire, FDNY says
local.b: The fire at the Patterson Houses in Mott Haven killed an 11-year-old boy and critically injured four other people early Wednesday.
local.title: Lithium-ion battery caused Bronx fire that killed 10-year-old, FDNY says

local.h: NYPD promises tight NYC Marathon security
local.b: Drones, dogs, horses and helicopters will watch the race; Commissioner Jessica Tisch said there are "no known specific credible threats."
local.title: 60K runners, 2.5 million fans: NYPD promises tight security for NYC Marathon

local.h: Brooklyn's Third Avenue to get safety redesign
local.b: The city will replace traffic lanes with bike lanes and shorten crossings on 2.1 miles of Third Avenue in Sunset Park, two months after nurse Jiayi Zheng was killed by a hit-and-run driver.
local.title: Mamdani plans redesign of Brooklyn's Third Avenue after nurse killed in hit-and-run

local.h: Board delays vote on Tompkins Square overhaul
local.b: Community Board 3 put off its vote on the $10 million Tompkins Square Park update until next month after preservationists protested over the park's pull-up bars.
local.title: 'If this is what you want': East Village board halts vote on Tompkins Square overhaul

local.h: Trappes shooting suspect targeted Muslims, Africans
local.b: The 39-year-old suspect, who killed one person and wounded seven west of Paris, admitted targeting people who appeared Muslim or African, prosecutors said.
local.title: French shooting suspect deliberately targeted Muslims and Africans, says prosecutor

local.h: Yellow Vests plan third Paris march Oct. 31
local.b: The Yellow Vests and the CGT union have requested routes starting at Place de la Bastille for another day of cost-of-living protests on Saturday.

local.h: Most fake riot posts came from abroad, minister says
local.b: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said two-thirds of social media content linking the October 17th looting to immigration came from abroad.

local.h: BHV department store seeks bankruptcy protection
local.b: The landmark store opposite Paris City Hall, which employs 700 people, will remain open; the company called the procedure part of its relaunch, not its failure.

local.h: GEO Group gets $1.5B deal to run Tacoma ICE center
local.b: ICE awarded the private prison company a 10-year contract for the 1,635-bed Northwest ICE Processing Center despite reports of poor conditions.
local.title: Feds approve $1.5 billion contract for GEO Group to continue running Tacoma ICE center

local.h: Washington suicide deaths hit 25-year high
local.b: Nearly 1,400 people died by suicide in the state in 2025, the most in 25 years, according to new health department data.
local.title: 1,400 people died by suicide in Washington state last year, a record

local.h: Hobbs rebuffs claims of non-citizen voting
local.b: Secretary of State Steve Hobbs responded after two U.S. attorneys said they found more than 400 non-citizens on Washington voter rolls and asked officials to set aside matching ballots.
